o1.biggest_strength: Builds the whole series around the two retention habits (typed recurring task and second device) with a hand-off-ready at-a-glance table, platform branching and send rules, all traced to the brief's numbers.
o1.biggest_mistake: Drops Pro from onboarding entirely and then reuses email 2's recurring-task tip in email 5, so the same non-converters get a near-duplicate ask and there is no upgrade path left.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make email 5 a genuinely new step (a later, value-based Pro email for users who already have both habits) so all five emails teach something distinct.

o2.biggest_strength: Uses every trigger with a clear goal and worked-if measure per email, keeps Pro but moves it to day 14 for engaged users only, and adds a sensible 0.4% unsubscribe guardrail.
o2.biggest_mistake: The Pro email's goal is not tied to either retention habit, and the one-month holdout cannot measure day-30 retention for users who sign up late in that window.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep every email aimed at the two habits (Pro on a separate later track) and run the holdout for eight weeks so day-30 retention is actually measurable.

reason: Output 1's at-a-glance table, send rules and platform split make it something I can hand to my team tomorrow, and every email drives one of the two habits; Output 2 is close but its Pro email pulls away from that focus and its one-month holdout can't really measure day-30 retention.
